pr_title: [Fix #12557] Make server mode aware of auto-restart for `bundle update`
pr_body:
Resolves #12557.

Currently, the server mode only auto-restarts due to incompatible versions of RuboCop core. This PR will enable auto-restart when the SHA1 value of Gemfile.lock becomes incompatible. If Gemfile.lock is missing, it will continue to refer to the RuboCop core version as before.

The advantage is that it can cover cases of version incompatibility caused by `bundle update`, which will likely cover many scenarios like those in #12557.

The disadvantage is that the server mode may become slightly slower. However, it is unlikely to be slow enough for users to notice. The trade-off is considered acceptable.

In the future, it might be possible to detect changes in rubocop configuration as well, but for now, I'd like to see how things go with this change.

-----------------

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] The PR relates to *only* one subject with a clear title and description in grammatically correct, complete sentences.
* [x] Wrote [good commit messages][1].
* [x] Commit message starts with `[Fix #issue-number]` (if the related issue exists).
* [x] Feature branch is up-to-date with `master` (if not - rebase it).
* [x] Squashed related commits together.
* [x] Added tests.
* [x] Ran `bundle exec rake default`. It executes all tests and runs RuboCop on its own code.
* [x] Added an entry (file) to the [changelog folder](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/changelog/) named `{change_type}_{change_description}.md` if the new code introduces user-observable changes. See [changelog entry format](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entry-format) for details.

[1]: https://chris.beams.io/posts/git-commit/

issue_context.title: Wrong version of extensions loaded with 1.59.0?
issue_context.body:
## Expected behavior

With same exact Gemfile and Gemfile.lock, with updated rubocop extensions, rubocop is loading the wrong version dependencies. (see version info below)

This is true even if the other versions are fully uninstalled (gem uninstall rubocop-performance and bundle exec gem uninstall rubocop-performance before bundle install again)

## Actual behavior

Gemfile has this in it:

```
  gem "rubocop", "~> 1.59.0"
  gem "rubocop-capybara", "~> 2.19.0"
  gem "rubocop-graphql", "~> 1.4.0"
  gem "rubocop-minitest", "~> 0.34.1"
  gem "rubocop-performance", "~> 1.20.0"
  gem "rubocop-rails", "~> 2.23.0"
  gem "rubocop-rake", "~> 0.6.0"
 ```

and this in .rubocop.yml:

```
require:
  - rubocop-rails
  - rubocop-minitest
  - rubocop-performance
  - rubocop-rake
  - rubocop-graphql
  - rubocop-capybara
```

## Steps to reproduce the problem

with above gemfile, have multiple people run:

```
bundle install
bundle exec rubocop -V
```

## RuboCop version

This is what it should be per Gemfile.lock and there on a number of our machines:

```
1.59.0 (using Parser 3.2.2.4, rubocop-ast 1.30.0, running on ruby 3.0.6) [arm64-darwin22]
  - rubocop-capybara 2.19.0
  - rubocop-graphql 1.4.0
  - rubocop-minitest 0.34.1
  - rubocop-performance 1.20.0
  - rubocop-rails 2.23.0
  - rubocop-rake 0.6.0
 ```

But others are seeing:

```
1.59.0 (using Parser 3.2.2.4, rubocop-ast 1.30.0, running on ruby 3.0.6) +server [arm64-darwin22]
  - rubocop-capybara 2.19.0
  - rubocop-graphql 1.4.0
  - rubocop-minitest 0.33.0
  - rubocop-performance 1.19.1
  - rubocop-rails 2.22.2
  - rubocop-rake 0.6.0
```

You can further see this in debug mode:

When working, it states:

```

configuration from /Users/REDACTED/.rbenv/versions/3.0.6/lib/ruby/gems/3.0.0/gems/rubocop-minitest-0.34.1/config/default.yml
```

comments:
I ran into the same bug and got very, very confused. I discovered that running `--no-server` had the behavior I expected. This makes sense because if you're using `--server` it could cache the old versions. Otherwise I was unclear how this could possibly even be happening.

Seems like `rubocop` needs to detect that dependency versions have changed and restart in that case.

I have encountered the same problem in using `--server`, and there we were to execute `bundle exec rubocop --restart-server` as a workaround. (To be precise, my project uses `rubocop --server` in our pre-commit hook, and a member who is not very familiar with rubocop got stuck with this problem.)

In our example, the RuboCop server is running with rubocop-capybara 2.19.0, which was changed to 2.20.0 by `git pull`. The `Capybara/RedundantWithinFind` cop that was added there was referenced in the new .rubocop_todo.yml, which caused the following error:

```
Error: unrecognized cop or department Capybara/RedundantWithinFind found in .rubocop_todo.yml
Did you mean `Capybara/NegationMatcher`?
```

I think this is a common use case, so we should make sure to check even the dependent gem versions, as dgollahon said.

https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/3ce4fbfa8865740d963772d6ecd926cf9c5b0893/lib/rubocop/server/client_command/exec.rb#L33-L46

At this phase, rubocop may not yet know the gems it depends on, and may not have loaded them, so it doesn't seem easy to find out the versions, though. Furthermore, it is easy to check the version of dependent gems on the server side, but on the client side, it is a bit difficult to do so, since the client does not load such things to speed up the process. (I'm thinking that if we only want to check the versions, it won't take that long)

Note that if you are using a custom cop in your project, they are not versioned, so if you have checked the version of the dependent gem, there will be cases where it will not work. If there is a feature in .rubocop.yml that allows you to set an arbitrary cache key, I think it will work well in such cases, as follows:

```yaml
# .rubocop.yml
ServerCacheKey: v2
```

Or if rubocop will be able to check the dependent gem versions, it would be good to implement the custom cops in the project as an internal gem.
Got the same behavior in Rubocop `1.64.1` with `rubocop-shopify` gem.
@koic Not sure we can do much about this, but perhaps we can at least document some of the things @r7kamura mentioned.
It’s pretty [well documented](https://docs.rubocop.org/rubocop/usage/server.html#restart-server), but a surprising behaviour nevertheless.
FYI, I've opened PR #13004, which will likely cover many cases of this issue.

review_comments: Does it make sense to `read.grep(/rubocop/)` to avoid restarting on unrelated updates?

Unrelated is a bit fuzzy here. For example, if I conservatively update the `parser` gem because a new ruby version released I'd still want it to restart rubocop.

Personally I think its safer to keep it like that, having it run more closely to how it would do without server mode.

Yes. It is prioritize that the environment can be aligned even when updating dependent gems that don't match `/rubocop/`, to prevent user confusion. Especially since it is not possible to know in advance which gems 3rd party gem depends on. Also, since `bundle update` occurs less frequently than `rubocop` is run, it has been decided that updating the entire Gemfile.lock to SHA1 is a trade-off that makes sense.
